messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: kv-cache size on batch-pool-7 exceeded 4x baseline, request latency spike + elevated 503s observed. Trigger: continuous-batching window increase (recent rollout)

maya (oncall): I'm seeing a bunch of 5xx traces tied to kv-store misses and OOM on the batcher containers. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/obs/kvcache?span=15m

raj (sre): on it. telling pager now. attaching initial graphs. looks like prefix cache churn + a tokenizer mismatch on the new prompt-template rollout.

olivia (mlinfra): Confirmed. New template change introduced additional prefix tokens for a small subset of prompts. The tokenizer update in the same deploy changed token boundaries -> different prefix hashes. Combined with increased continuous-batching window, we got a hotset of long-lived KV entries + KV eviction pressure.

ben (runtime): Symptoms: sustained high KV store size, frequent prefix regenerations, continuous-batching holding onto large KV caches per request group => memory pressure on GPU workers. Rapid latency cliff for requests that hit that hot prefix.

sam (support): Customer impact: a handful of PLG customers reported timeouts and failed embedding calls around 08:42 UTC. Tix: #5482, #5483. Not widespread but high-impact for real-time products.

maya (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) revert continuous-batching window to prior value 2) disable new prompt-template rollout (canary) 3) force-prefix-invalidation for problematic templates 4) scale batch-pool down for testing. Who can run the first two?

ben (runtime): I can push a fast rollback for batching config. Will patch the runtime config and restart batcher fleet gradually. Patch cmd: `kubectl -n inference set env ds/batcher CONT_BATCH_WINDOW=30ms --record` then monitor.

olivia (mlinfra): I'll rollback the prompt-template canary in the model-config service. PR ID: `mc/PR-7821` -> reverting tokenization-affecting changes. Canary to 0% now.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollout/rollback batcher-config -> batch-pool-7..9 (3/10), expected low disruption. Link: https://deploys.redwood/rollouts/1345

maya (oncall): Doing controlled rollback. Adding `--drain` to avoid in-flight request drop.

raj (sre): Also recommend immediate KV scrub for affected prefix namespace. We'll run a targeted TTL sweep and increase KV eviction aggressiveness temporarily: `kvctl sweep --prefix prompt-template:v2 --max-evict 5000`

ben (runtime): Executed config rollback on 7..9. Early signs: CPU stable, memory trending down. Latency improving in 1-3 minute windows.

sam (support): Notifying impacted customers that we're investigating and rolling back; PS is tracking.

lina (product): Can we get a short customer-facing blurb? "We experienced elevated latency and errors affecting text generation for some customers between 08:38-09:05 UTC. Root cause: interaction between a prompt-template change and batching config. Mitigation in progress."

maya (oncall): Agreed. Sam please send that.

sam (support): Sent. Tickets updated.

deploy-bot: Deploy finished: rollback batcher-config (10/10) — success.

olivia (mlinfra): Canary rollback applied (mc/PR-7821 reverted). Prompt-template traffic at 0%.

raj (sre): Running KV sweep now. Output snippet:
```
INFO kvctl: scanned 120k keys, evicted 9.2k, reclaimed 1.7GB
WARN some nodes reported transient errors — retrying
```

ben (runtime): Post-rollback metrics: kv-cache size down ~65% vs peak; p50 latency back to baseline, p95 down from 4.1s to 320ms on affected routes. No further 503 surge.

maya (oncall): Handoff: I'm going to hand to @raj for postmortem and follow-up actions. Oncall shift ends in 40m.

raj (sre): Taking it. Immediate action items: 1) postmortem writeup 2) add tokenizer compatibility gate to template PRs 3) add an automated check: if kv-cache growth >2x in 5m after config change, auto-disable continuous-batching and notify oncall 4) refine prefix invalidation tooling.

olivia (mlinfra): For 2): propose adding a deterministic tokenization diff step in CI: given old/new templates, ensure hash(prefixes) stable for existing prompt set or fail. I'll draft the CI job.

ben (runtime): For 3) I can add a guard in the router: short-circuit continuous-batching on memory pressure KPI crossing a threshold. Will open PR.

lina (product): Metrics to include in postmortem: customer impact list, revenue-affecting requests, rollback timeline, number of affected keys, and expected mitigations for UX.

sam (support): Adding customer case IDs to the incident doc. Sending closure emails once we have confirmed stability for 24h.

raj (sre): Quick root cause summary for now: tokenizer boundary change in a prompt-template can alter prefix hashes. With an expanded continuous-batching window, that caused key churn + an unexpectedly large hotset of prefixes to coexist, exhausting KV memory and causing request timeouts.

maya (oncall): FYI: no data exfil or PII exposure. KV eviction removed stale keys; we did not persist new data outside normal logging.

deploy-bot: Noted. Incident severity: Sev2 -> decreased to Sev3 after rollback and KV scrub.

raj (sre): Follow-ups (owner):
- olivia: tokenizer-diff-ci (ETA 1 week)
- ben: batching-memory-guard (ETA 3 days)
- maya/raj: postmortem doc (ETA EOD)
- devops: add KV metrics alert for rapid growth (ETA 2 days)

maya (oncall): Leaving final note: thanks all for quick turnaround. We contained customer impact and rolled back risky canary. Will post postmortem channel once done. :thumbsup:

sam (support): Closing interim incident thread, moving to postmortem doc.

incident-bot: Incident update: severity->SEV3, status->stabilized, link-> https://incidents.redwood/3012345678
